verdict.headline: Likely ball fault detected in rotating equipment bearing
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays a strong, steady vibration band at low frequencies with repeating harmonic lines across higher frequencies. This distinctive pattern typically indicates repeated impact from a damaged or pitted rolling ball striking the bearing raceway.
verdict.likely_cause: Surface fatigue, spalling, or debris contamination damaging the rolling balls inside the bearing.
verdict.risk: Ignoring this will lead to bearing seizure, potentially damaging the shaft and causing an unscheduled motor failure.
next_steps: Check bearing housing temperature and listen for audible grinding or rumbling
Inspect lubrication quality and check for metal particulate in the grease
Schedule a replacement of the bearing assembly during planned downtime

verdict.headline: Potential bearing cage wear detected on rotating equipment
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays energy concentrated almost exclusively at the very bottom edge in the lowest frequency range, with virtually no high-frequency vibration activity. Bearing cage defects typically produce low-frequency, sub-synchronous vibration signatures rather than the high-frequency impact bursts seen with ball or raceway defects. This distinct low-frequency profile aligns well with the model's cage fault classification.
verdict.likely_cause: Looseness, cracking, or inadequate lubrication in the bearing retainer cage separating the rolling elements.
verdict.risk: A deteriorating cage can break and cause the rolling elements to jam, resulting in catastrophic bearing seizure and shaft damage.
next_steps: Inspect the bearing housing for abnormal noise, excess heat, or discolored lubricant.
Perform a narrow-band vibration FFT check to verify fundamental train frequency (FTF) harmonics.
Schedule bearing replacement before the cage fractures and seizes the equipment.

verdict.headline: Suspected rolling element (ball) damage in the machine bearing
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays distinct, persistent horizontal energy bands concentrated in the lower frequency range. These stable harmonic lines indicate repetitive impacts typical of damaged rolling elements striking the races during rotation. This clear harmonic signature confirms mechanical wear rather than normal operational vibration.
verdict.likely_cause: Spalling, surface pitting, or micro-cracking on one or more of the bearing balls.
verdict.risk: Untreated ball damage will accelerate wear across the entire assembly, risking complete bearing seizure and shaft damage.
next_steps: Inspect bearing housing for abnormal heat, audible grinding, or excessive vibration.
Examine lubricant for contamination, metal particles, or breakdown.
Schedule bearing replacement during upcoming maintenance before total mechanical seizure.

verdict.headline: Bearing is operating normally with no signs of damage.
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays a clean, uniform background with acoustic energy confined strictly to the baseline at the very bottom. There are no high-frequency friction bands, periodic impacts, or harmonic lines typical of bearing fault modes. This clean profile confirms the equipment is running smoothly.
verdict.likely_cause: Normal, healthy mechanical rotation under steady-state operating conditions.
verdict.risk: No current risk exists under standard running conditions.
next_steps: Log baseline vibration reading in the equipment history record.
Continue standard periodic monitoring and routine lubrication schedules.

verdict.headline: Probable internal bearing raceway wear detected
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays persistent vibration bands concentrated at the lowest frequencies with faint harmonic excitation higher up. This steady harmonic pattern is characteristic of rolling elements repeatedly striking a defect on the rotating inner ring.
verdict.likely_cause: Surface fatigue, spalling, or micro-cracking along the bearing's inner raceway due to normal wear or poor lubrication.
verdict.risk: Neglecting the fault will accelerate bearing breakdown, potentially leading to shaft damage or sudden motor seizure.
next_steps: Perform an acoustic and thermal inspection around the bearing housing to check for overheating or grinding
Inspect the grease condition for metal particulates and replenish lubrication if low
Schedule a scheduled bearing replacement before running the unit under peak load

verdict.headline: Bearing outer ring is degrading and vibrating excessively
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays distinct, persistent horizontal energy bands concentrated in the low-to-mid frequency zones. Because the outer ring is fixed in the bearing housing, rolling elements strike the defect at a steady rate, creating these strong, continuous vibration signatures. This steady harmonic pattern strongly aligns with a developing outer race flaw.
verdict.likely_cause: Metal fatigue and surface spalling on the outer bearing raceway due to prolonged runtime, improper lubrication, or shaft misalignment.
verdict.risk: The defect will accelerate, leading to complete bearing seizure, motor shaft damage, and unplanned equipment shutdown.
next_steps: Inspect the bearing housing for abnormal heat, audible grinding, or loose mounting bolts.
Verify lubrication levels and check for metal shavings or grease degradation.
Schedule a planned shutdown to replace the worn bearing assembly before complete failure occurs.

verdict.headline: Significant cracking identified in the concrete surface
verdict.explanation: Multiple tiles clearly show wide, dark fracture lines cutting across the concrete. These heavy cracks indicate noticeable material separation rather than minor surface blemishes or dirt.
verdict.likely_cause: Structural settling, thermal expansion cycles, or excessive load-bearing stress.
verdict.risk: Unsealed cracks permit moisture penetration, accelerating rebar corrosion and leading to spalling or structural failure.
next_steps: Locate the marked concrete section on-site and measure the crack width and depth.
Inspect the opposite side and surrounding areas for signs of movement, displacement, or water infiltration.
Have a structural specialist evaluate the crack to determine if epoxy injection or structural remediation is required.

verdict.headline: Visible crack observed running through the concrete surface.
verdict.explanation: The image clearly shows a continuous dark fracture line spanning across the concrete material. The sharp, jagged edges and depth contrast confirm an active surface crack rather than superficial discoloration or dirt. This directly corroborates the classifier's positive detection.
verdict.likely_cause: Drying shrinkage, thermal cycling, or foundation settling stresses over time.
verdict.risk: Unsealed cracks permit water and contaminants to penetrate, potentially accelerating concrete deterioration and corroding internal reinforcing steel.
next_steps: Measure and log the width and total length of the crack.
Inspect the area for signs of water infiltration or spalling around the fissure.
Clean out debris and seal with an appropriate structural epoxy or elastomeric sealant.

verdict.headline: Significant open crack identified in the concrete surface
verdict.explanation: The image clearly shows a wide, continuous fracture cutting across the concrete with deep shadowing along the break. The jagged, separated edges indicate a through-crack rather than minor surface crazing. This strongly confirms the automated classifier's crack detection.
verdict.likely_cause: Structural shifting, foundation settlement, or excessive tensile load on the concrete.
verdict.risk: Moisture can penetrate the crack to corrode internal steel reinforcement, leading to spalling and serious structural weakening.
next_steps: Photograph and measure the full length and width of the crack for baseline tracking.
Check surrounding walls, slabs, or joints for corresponding movement or secondary cracking.
Have a structural engineer evaluate load conditions and specify an epoxy injection or reinforcement repair.

verdict.headline: Concrete surface is sound with no visible cracking
verdict.explanation: The inspection tiles display normal surface texture, minor aggregate speckling, and standard finish variations across all sections. There are no continuous lines, fractures, or separating fissures visible anywhere in the grid. The high confidence rating for an undamaged surface is well supported.
verdict.likely_cause: Normal surface texture and material variations without structural distress.
verdict.risk: No current risk exists as the concrete integrity appears intact.
next_steps: Log the inspection scan as clear in building records
Maintain standard scheduled visual inspections

verdict.headline: No structural cracks detected on this surface section
verdict.explanation: The image displays a uniform concrete texture with typical fine aggregate patterns and isolated minor surface flecks. There are no linear fissures, fractures, or crack paths visible anywhere across the tile. The classifier correctly identifies this area as sound and uncracked.
verdict.likely_cause: Normal concrete surface finish with minor cosmetic surface pitting or aggregate variation.
verdict.risk: No structural or moisture ingress risk is present in this section.
next_steps: Log this tile as clear in the inspection records
Proceed with regular scheduled maintenance inspections

verdict.headline: Concrete surface is sound with no signs of cracking
verdict.explanation: The image shows a uniform concrete texture without any linear fractures, separations, or fissures. Minor surface mottling and tiny aggregate pores are normal characteristics of cured concrete. The visual inspection confirms the classifier's assessment that the area is intact.
verdict.likely_cause: Normal, healthy concrete surface with standard surface porosity.
verdict.risk: There is no present structural or cosmetic risk.
next_steps: Log the inspection as clear with no defects found
Maintain standard scheduled visual inspections

verdict.headline: Motor bearing is deteriorating and requires replacement
verdict.explanation: The audio sensor on the left displays sharp, distinct harmonic fault frequencies across multiple bands. Simultaneously, the vibration sensor on the right reveals repetitive shock patterns characteristic of rolling element impacts. These synchronized signals strongly confirm localized bearing damage.
verdict.likely_cause: Spalling, raceway pitting, or severe mechanical wear within the bearing assembly.
verdict.risk: Ignoring the defect will lead to complete bearing seizure, shaft damage, and unexpected equipment shutdown.
next_steps: Check the bearing housing temperature using an infrared thermometer.
Inspect the bearing for proper lubrication and signs of metal contamination.
Schedule and complete a bearing replacement before full mechanical failure occurs.

verdict.headline: Equipment operating normally with no detected mechanical faults
verdict.explanation: Both the acoustic and vibration spectrograms show smooth, steady horizontal lines typical of standard baseline motor operation. There are no sudden impacts, strong irregular harmonics, or high-frequency friction bursts that would indicate wear or damage. This confirms the machine is running within expected normal parameters.
verdict.likely_cause: Routine steady-state operation of motor and bearings under normal load.
verdict.risk: No immediate risk; ignoring healthy baseline data will not harm equipment, though periodic monitoring should continue.
next_steps: Continue standard automated monitoring schedule.
Log baseline acoustic and vibration signatures for future reference.
Perform standard scheduled visual and lubrication inspections as planned.

verdict.headline: Drive shaft or coupling misalignment detected
verdict.explanation: The audio spectrogram reveals pronounced, evenly spaced horizontal harmonic lines across multiple multiples of the motor rotation speed. This persistent multi-harmonic signature alongside elevated low-frequency vibration is typical of parallel or angular shaft misalignment.
verdict.likely_cause: The motor shaft and driven shaft are out of alignment due to settling, loose mounting bolts, or thermal growth.
verdict.risk: Uncorrected misalignment accelerates wear on bearings, mechanical seals, and couplings, eventually leading to catastrophic mechanical failure.
next_steps: Inspect the flexible coupling and mounting bolts for physical play or damage.
Perform a laser shaft alignment check between the motor and driven rotor.
Shim and re-torque the motor feet to correct angular and offset tolerances.

verdict.headline: Rotor is significantly out of balance, causing strong low-frequency vibrations.
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays intense, steady horizontal bands concentrated in the lower frequency region across both acoustic and vibration sensors. This constant energy at fundamental rotational speeds is a classic sign of uneven weight distribution on a spinning shaft. Both sensors agree with high confidence, confirming mechanical unbalance rather than random electrical noise.
verdict.likely_cause: Uneven dirt or dust accumulation, physical wear, or a missing balancing weight on the rotor.
verdict.risk: Ignoring the imbalance will rapidly degrade the bearings, damage seals, and potentially cause catastrophic shaft or motor failure.
next_steps: Lock out the equipment and inspect the rotor or fan blades for debris buildup and damage.
Clean the rotating assembly thoroughly and check for missing balancing weights.
Perform dynamic balancing and verify vibration levels return to baseline before returning to service.

verdict.headline: Motor bearing shows clear signs of wear and mechanical degradation
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays persistent low-frequency vibration tones alongside elevated broadband noise across the frequency range. This continuous high-frequency hash combined with harmonic banding is characteristic of rolling-element impacts inside a damaged bearing. These patterns strongly support the high-confidence classifier reading.
verdict.likely_cause: Frictional wear, surface spalling, or degraded lubrication within the bearing race or rolling elements.
verdict.risk: Complete bearing seizure could damage the drive shaft, overheat the motor, and cause sudden equipment failure.
next_steps: Inspect the equipment bearing housing for abnormal heat, grease leakage, or audible grinding.
Check bearing lubrication levels and apply fresh grease if dry.
Schedule a bearing replacement before full mechanical seizure occurs.

verdict.headline: Equipment operating normally with no detected mechanical or fluid faults
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays a consistent, smooth acoustic baseline with no sharp harmonic frequency bands or chaotic broadband bursts. This uniform acoustic signature indicates smooth mechanical rotation without impact, friction, or turbulent leak noise.
verdict.likely_cause: Normal baseline machinery or pipe operation under steady operating conditions.
verdict.risk: No operational risk detected under current operating conditions.
next_steps: Archive this recording as an acoustic baseline for future comparison
Proceed with regular scheduled equipment monitoring

verdict.headline: Equipment is operating normally with no detected faults
verdict.explanation: The acoustic reading shows a smooth baseline profile concentrated in normal low frequencies. There are no sharp harmonic ridges, sidebands, or broadband high-frequency hissing that would indicate mechanical failure or pipe leaks. The machine or pipe appears to be running in healthy condition.
verdict.likely_cause: Normal operational baseline vibration and acoustic signature.
verdict.risk: No risk identified under current operating conditions.
next_steps: Log current recording as a healthy operational baseline
Continue standard periodic monitoring as scheduled

verdict.headline: Motor shaft and coupled equipment are out of alignment
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays multiple strong, evenly spaced horizontal harmonic lines across the frequency spectrum. This signature pattern is typical of shaft misalignment in rotating machinery, producing repeated mechanical impulses at multiples of the rotational speed. The clear distribution of energy across multiple harmonics strongly supports the classifier's diagnosis.
verdict.likely_cause: Angular or parallel misalignment between the motor shaft and driven pump or fan coupling.
verdict.risk: Prolonged operation under misalignment will cause rapid bearing wear, coupling failure, and eventual motor breakdown.
next_steps: Schedule a visual inspection of the motor-to-load coupling for wear or looseness.
Use a laser alignment tool or dial indicators to verify and correct angular and parallel alignment.
Inspect motor mounting bolts, base integrity, and check for soft foot before final torquing.

verdict.headline: Active water pipe leak detected
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays a continuous, steady acoustic band across mid-range frequencies without periodic machine harmonics. This diffuse, uninterrupted noise signature strongly corresponds to turbulent flow from pressurized water escaping a pipe.
verdict.likely_cause: A pinhole rupture, joint failure, or cracked fitting along the pressurized piping.
verdict.risk: Continuous water escape leads to structural rot, mold infestation, and costly secondary water damage.
next_steps: Trace the piping run near the sensor using an acoustic listening stick or thermal imaging camera.
Verify baseline water meter flow when equipment is inactive to confirm continuous leakage.
Isolate the affected branch line and replace the compromised pipe section.

verdict.headline: Motor or fan rotor appears significantly unbalanced
verdict.explanation: The spectrogram displays clear, continuous horizontal bands concentrated in the lower frequency range, representing steady rotational harmonics. This steady periodic energy pattern is a hallmark acoustic signature of rotor mass imbalance. The high model confidence and distinct harmonic lines strongly support the diagnosis.
verdict.likely_cause: Uneven weight distribution on the rotating shaft, fan wheel, or pump impeller due to dirt buildup, wear, or a thrown balance weight.
verdict.risk: Persistent vibration will rapidly wear out bearings and mechanical seals, eventually causing premature equipment failure or shutdown.
next_steps: Inspect the fan impeller or pump rotor for dirt buildup, damage, or loose components.
Clean the rotating assembly and check shaft runout and mounting tightness.
Perform dynamic field balancing or replace damaged rotating parts if vibration persists.

verdict.headline: Motor is severely overheating due to lack of airflow from the cooling fan
verdict.explanation: The thermal image shows widespread, intense heat across the entire ribbed motor housing compared to the cooler surroundings. Without airflow from the rear fan, heat generated by standard operation cannot dissipate and builds up uniformly along the cooling fins. This confirms that the external cooling system is impaired or failing.
verdict.likely_cause: Broken, loose, or obstructed cooling fan blades under the rear shroud preventing forced air cooling.
verdict.risk: Continued operation without cooling will degrade winding insulation, cause an electrical short, and lead to complete motor burnout.
next_steps: Safely shut down and lock out power to the motor.
Inspect the rear fan cowl for physical blockage, debris, or broken fan blades.
Confirm the fan turns freely with the shaft and replace damaged fan components before restarting.

verdict.headline: Motor shows normal thermal distribution with no signs of overheating
verdict.explanation: The infrared image shows a uniform, cool color profile across the motor casing and drive end without concentrated hot spots. There are no localized bright regions indicative of stator winding faults or bearing failure. This confirms normal heat dissipation and balanced operation.
verdict.likely_cause: Normal, balanced electrical and mechanical operating conditions.
verdict.risk: No immediate risk; the motor is operating well within safe thermal thresholds.
next_steps: Log thermal scan to document baseline operating conditions
Continue standard routine preventative maintenance schedule
Perform periodic follow-up scans under peak operational load

verdict.headline: Severe motor overheating caused by an internal electrical short circuit
verdict.explanation: The thermal scan shows intense, abnormal heat concentrated directly along the ribbed stator housing in the middle of the motor. This uniform overheating of the core while the rear fan shroud remains cooler indicates high internal current rather than poor airflow. These visual signs strongly align with an internal winding insulation failure.
verdict.likely_cause: Degraded winding insulation causing an internal turn-to-turn or phase short circuit in the stator.
verdict.risk: Complete motor burnout, tripped breakers, and a potential electrical fire hazard.
next_steps: Safely de-energize and lock out the motor immediately
Perform winding resistance and insulation resistance (megger) testing
Replace or rewind the damaged motor

verdict.headline: Motor is dangerously overheating due to a seized or stalled rotor
verdict.explanation: The thermal image shows severe, intense heat concentrated entirely across the central stator body. When a motor rotor is locked or stuck, it draws excessive electrical current without rotating, causing rapid and extreme heat buildup across the motor core. The lack of air movement from the fan worsens the overheating.
verdict.likely_cause: Mechanical jamming of the driven load, seized internal bearings, or an electrical stall condition.
verdict.risk: Immediate catastrophic failure of the motor windings and high risk of an electrical fire.
next_steps: Cut electrical power to the motor immediately to prevent winding burnout.
Lock out and tag out the equipment breaker.
Manually inspect the shaft to check for mechanical seizure or binding in the connected load.
